HoyoToon 5.2.7, https://github.com/Hoyotoon/HoyoToon
Upstream commit d9e5ca2f312bf16fba89dee67d32c08b482dcda4.
Authors: Meliodas, Manashiku, Tay and HoyoToon contributors.
GPL-3.0: see LICENSE.txt. These are STAFF URP adaptations, not an official URP release.

Separate Genshin, Star Rail, Zenless Zone Zero and Wuthering Waves implementations.
Game HLSL include files retain upstream contents. ShaderLab changes provide URP
engine inputs, pass tags, and a source UV/alpha-coverage wrapper. The external
HoyoToon custom inspector is not included. StaffURPBridge translates Built-in APIs.

The runtime PMX adapter copies source albedo, tint, culling, UV transform and cutoff.
It uses Base material defaults because the existing PMX sources do not supply
per-game SDF/packed maps. Optional game outlines are disabled on these PMX materials:
their vertex data and scale do not match the game-authored outline convention.
No generated neutral masks or custom Smooth/TwoTone branch is applied.
At user request, the previous brightness/color-temperature settings are retained:
exposure 0.8, neutral direct/probe illumination, and white ZZZ post-tint values.
These controls live in the URP/surface adapter and material settings; each game
retains its own shading equations.

This is a six-mode shader comparison, not reconstruction of the original games'
complete character materials. Game-specific face/hair setup requires matching maps.
URP schedules base, stencil and outline passes. Additional point/spot lights are
evaluated in the base pass through each game's original ForwardAdd fragment
equations (generated StaffAdditionalLight.hlsl), using URP light attenuation and
shadows. Specialized game effects require further integration and source data.
The old HoyoToonMMD folder/template is retained for existing asset references, but
CharacterToonToggle no longer reads or uses that template.
